info.name: TallyTalk - Telegram Webhook
info.description:
Manual test coverage for POST /webhook/telegram: the two security gates (secret token, user allowlist) and normal message processing. Mirrors tests/telegram-webhook.test.js. Requires the backend running locally (npm run dev / npm start) and the 'TallyTalk Local' environment selected.

Note: the two "allowed user" requests call the real LLM (Anthropic) and, on success, produce a real conversation draft/Telegram reply — that's expected, not a bug. Nothing in this collection sends a Confirm callback, so Tally is never written to.

request.description: No X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header at all. Expect 401 {"error":"unauthorized"}. No reply is sent, nothing is queued.
Header present but wrong. Expect 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} — identical response to the missing-secret case, deliberately, so a prober learns nothing.

Correct secret, but from.id is NOT in TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS. Expect 200 {"ok":true} (Telegram must not be told to retry), but no Telegram reply is sent and no LLM call happens. Check the backend log for 'Rejected update from user not on allowlist'.

exec: pm.test('body is ok:true', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.eql({ ok: true }));

request.description: There is no dedicated /start handler anywhere in this codebase — it flows through as an ordinary text message into the LLM extractor. Expect 200 {"ok":true}. This calls the real Anthropic API; a real Telegram reply is sent back to this chat id.

exec: pm.test('body is ok:true', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.eql({ ok: true }));

request.description: A realistic transaction message from an allowed user. Expect 200 {"ok":true}, plus a real Telegram reply carrying the extraction preview (or a follow-up question) sent to this chat id. This calls the real Anthropic API and reads Tally masters read-only — it does NOT post anything to Tally (that only happens on a Confirm button callback, which this collection deliberately never sends).

exec: pm.test('body is ok:true', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.eql({ ok: true }));
